log.msg: THE ROUTING TRAP, solved the way the site already solves it — and the brief's framing was one step off. `ai/2026-08-17/page.js` did not exist; every OTHER day (08-08 .. 08-16) has one, declared in `ai/page.js`'s `children:`, and `ai/page.js`'s `route()` is the fallback for a day that has NOT written one. So the fix was not a defensive hack: it was writing the missing day page. `Page.child()` resolves memory -> route() -> filesystem probe, and route() sees UNDECLARED names only, so declaring `report` in the day page's `children:` makes the probe fire and the AITask route can never claim it. Verified by CLICKING, not by loading the url: /framework/ai/ -> the 2026-08-17 card -> the report, three hops, title `Today, ranked`, and a sibling task dir (`ui-wall`) still routes to the AITask viewer unchanged. Zero console errors, zero failed requests.

TWO FILES TOUCHED OUTSIDE MY TASK DIR, both minimal: `ai/page.js`'s `children:` string gained `2026-08-17` at the front (one word), and `ai/2026-08-17/page.js` is NEW — the day page every other day already has, carrying the same `route()`/`preview()`/`dashboard()` shape as 2026-08-16's, plus one lead line linking the report. Nothing else in `ai/` changed.

MEASURED, after two rounds of fixes: **0 high findings at 390, 1280, 1920 and 3440**. rate() 74/C at 390, 86/B at 1280, 84/B at 1920, 87/B at 3440, with **width-used 0.86 / 0.88 / 0.92 / 0.93** — the prime objective, and the band that was blind until this morning. The 390 C is `measure` reading 37.4 characters, which is what a 390 screen gives any page on this site. Remaining: one med (`rhythm` on a `p.md`, measuring gaps between INLINE children — false-positive class 1) and lows that are the site-wide `--measure` decision and a 3.3px grid rounding.

A REAL BUG THE TOOL CAUGHT ON THIS PAGE, and it is the kind that never throws: `hit-size` reported `a.report-frame` as **334x2px, twice** — a lazy `` with no intrinsic size leaves its link 2px tall until the bytes arrive, so the whole report reflows under the reader as it scrolls. Fixed by giving every shot its PNG's real `width`/`height` (3440x1000, 3440x1900, 3440x1440, 1280x1080), which is what reserves the box. The high disappeared at every width. `shots.js` now takes `[src, [w, h], caption]` and the dimension is NOT optional.

THE CHROME COSTS THIS PAGE MORE THAN ITS OWN CSS DOES, confirming what human-ranking logged and did not fix. Every page under `/framework/ai/` mounts in `ext/catalog`'s region beside the `ai-index-rail`, which is `flex: 0 0 min(34em, 45%)` (`ai.css`) — so the report gets **506px of a 1280 viewport** and ~2280 of 3440. At 1280 the before/after pairs therefore stack rather than sit side by side; that is the rail's width, not this page's layout. Left alone deliberately: `--rail` and `container()` are both real seams, and both change how EVERY task page under `ai/` behaves. Second independent sighting of the same finding today.

ONE PAIR IS MISSING AND THE PAGE SAYS SO RATHER THAN FAKING IT: `layouts-redesign` wrote its before shots as `before-390/1280/3440.png`, and `ui-wall` wrote ITS before shots to the same three filenames five hours later. The layouts wall's before state is gone. The report shows the after (`wall-3440.png`, the whole 29-card catalog in one frame) with the measured numbers beside it and names the collision in the caption. Worth a convention: a shot filename should carry its subject, not just its width.

RANKING, and the reasoning behind it. Order is by what changes a decision, not by size of change: (1) the five that need Mike, first and unmissable, led by the ranking page because it is the ONLY thing that unblocks a whole program; (2) the two rebuilt walls, because they are the strongest images available and Mike's standing rule is that he wants to SEE results; (3) the instrument, because half the numbers quoted to him today turned out to be the ruler; (4) what is still weak — seven items, every one raised by the worker that did the work, including the caveat that cuts against Mike's own complaint (the layout TAB went 8 -> 10 controls even though the SCREEN went 3 -> 2); (5) everything else, five cards, one line each.

PRE-EXISTING 404 FOUND ON THE WAY, logged not fixed because it is outside my fence: `ai/2026-08-16/page.js` declares `children: "mastermind-layout"` but that directory holds only .md files and a task.jsonl — no `page.js`. So the filesystem probe 404s on **every load of /framework/ai/**, which is exactly the trap the new-task skill's §3 names (a declared child skips route() and 404s on the probe). One word to fix; whoever is next in ai/ should take it.

TOKEN ATTRIBUTION IS NOT SEPARABLE FOR THIS TASK, and that is the ledger finding rather than an omission: subagents inherit the parent's `session_id` AND its `transcript_path` (ledger-attribution proved both identical across two concurrent agents, with only `agent_id` differing), so summing the transcript would charge this task with the whole session's spend. Reporting the window movement instead — 30% → 46% of the 5h window across this task and everything else running in it concurrently, which is an upper bound, not my cost.
